name: defence
title: Defense program office
summary: Shows which requirements have passing tests and writes after-action reports. Runs only on models you host.

skills.name: cui-handling
skills.title: Protect controlled information
skills.blurb: Marks every file it writes as controlled and keeps its work inside this project.
skills.description: Use for every task in this workspace: all of its content is controlled unclassified information.
skills.body:
Treat everything in this workspace as Controlled Unclassified Information.

- Never send any of it to a website, search engine, or tool outside this workspace.
- Begin every file you write with the banner `CUI` on its own line and end it with `CUI`.
- Do not summarize CUI into a less protected form, such as an email draft or a public document, unless asked, and mark such a draft CUI too.
- If a task would need anything outside this workspace, stop and say what you would need.

skills.name: requirements-trace
skills.title: Trace requirements to tests
skills.blurb: Lists each requirement with its tests and whether it passed, failed or has no test.
skills.description: Use when asked to trace requirements to tests, find gaps in test coverage, or build a traceability matrix.
skills.body:
Build a requirements traceability matrix from the requirements and test evidence in the workspace.

- One row per requirement ID, in ID order: the requirement's short text, each test case that verifies it, the latest result of each, and a status of Verified, Failed or Not tested.
- A requirement is Verified only if every test tracing to it passed on its latest run.
- After the table, list failed and untested requirements with the reason, and any test that traces to no requirement.
- Save it as `traceability-matrix.md` with the CUI banner.

skills.name: after-action-report
skills.title: Write after-action reports
skills.blurb: Turns your exercise notes into a report: plan, events, causes and next steps.
skills.description: Use when asked for an after-action report, a lessons-learned review or an exercise debrief.
skills.body:
Write the report from the notes in the workspace, in four parts:

1. **What was planned**: the objectives and the plan as intended.
2. **What happened**: a timeline of what actually occurred, with times.
3. **Why it happened**: causes of each difference between plan and outcome, stated as findings, never blame of individuals.
4. **Sustain and improve**: what to keep doing and what to change, each with an owner role and a date to review.

Save it as `after-action-report.md` with the CUI banner.

# System requirements: field sensor relay (invented)

*All names, dates and identifiers in this file are invented for demonstration. It is not a real record.*

- **SR-001** The relay shall forward sensor messages to the command node within 2 seconds of receipt.
- **SR-002** The relay shall encrypt all traffic with AES-256.
- **SR-003** The relay shall operate for 72 hours on battery power.
- **SR-004** The relay shall buffer at least 10,000 messages when the command node is unreachable.
- **SR-005** The relay shall report its own health status every 60 seconds.
- **SR-006** The relay shall reject messages from unregistered sensors.

CUI

# Exercise NORTHERN RELAY notes (invented)

*All names, dates and identifiers in this file are invented for demonstration. It is not a real record.*

Plan: deploy 4 relays along the valley by 0600, establish link to command node by 0630, run message traffic for 12 h.

0540 Relays 1 to 3 deployed. Relay 4 team delayed, vehicle stuck at ford.
0615 Relay 4 deployed. Link established 0640, 10 min late.
0900 Command node lost power for 25 min. Relays buffered traffic; no message loss.
1310 Relay 2 battery warning, 28% remaining against 70% expected. Cold overnight.
1500 Relay 2 swapped. Traffic resumed after 6 min gap.
1830 End of exercise. 41,200 messages relayed, 0 lost, 3 delayed over 2 s.

Team comments: ford crossing was not on the route plan. Spare batteries were in the wrong vehicle. Buffering worked well.

CUI
